subject: AP Statistics
generated_at_note: Manually derived from a read-only Production audit, 2026-08-10. content_taxonomy_labels.primary_unit is null for all 10 items (taxonomy labeling never ran on this corpus) and content_item_versions.stem is generic boilerplate ('Answer all parts of the following question.') for every item, so the actual question topic was read from content_item_versions.stimulus and used as the module proxy instead. This is the one confound-check dimension available; no difficulty/form metadata differentiates these items (all frq_form='short').

topic_pairs.topic: descriptive stats / outliers and standardized scores (Unit 1 proxy)

selection_rule: Within each of the 5 naturally-occurring topic pairs, the item with the higher (or tied) verified-answer count was assigned to the held-out test pool (more ground-truth responses to test against); its topic-mate became the exemplar source. This is a within-topic split, not a random one -- given n=10 there was no basis for randomization, so pairing by shared topic was used to maximize exemplar relevance while keeping exemplar and test items strictly disjoint.

known_limitations: No taxonomy/difficulty metadata exists for this corpus; topic pairing was inferred by manually reading each item's stimulus text, not from a validated label -- treat the 'topic' field as a best-effort proxy, not ground truth.

Each held-out item is matched to exactly one exemplar item for the whole pilot (see Phase 2's exemplar-selection policy) -- this tests whether *this specific* exemplar helps, not exemplars in general.
n=5 held-out items/clusters is small; expect a wide confidence interval on any accuracy comparison (see REPORT.md's limitations section once Phase 5 runs).
